context:
Goal: the inbox holds your words and asks, not echoes of commands.
Problem (rule): the recorded debt inbox-saves-other-notices (the inbox saves notices that are not your messages) already names this; a new skip rule is a new ruling and is yours.
Based on (read): the consultant's reading of the Degen gap audit, gap 21 (not re-read by triage).
Departs from: main — the inbox saves a bash-input echo as an owner message that owes an item — it skips bash-input echoes and pastes with no instruction.
Waiting on: nothing is stopped; the consultant builds it on a yes.

options.gain: No empty items owed for echoes.
options.how: The inbox hook ignores a message that is only a bash-input echo, or a paste with no instruction beside it.
options.label: Skip bash-input echoes and bare pastes (recommended)
options.lose: A paste you meant as an ask, with no words, would not be saved.

options.label: Keep saving them
options.lose: Each echo owes an inbox line.

ref: consultant message 19:10 CST Nov 18, from the Degen gap audit (workflow wf_9ba2f097-22f); the audit's reads are the consultant's, not re-read by triage

shown.label: Skip bash-input echoes and bare pastes (recommended)

title: Should the feedback inbox skip echoes of commands you ran yourself and pastes with no instruction?
why: a removes empty items at the risk of one dropped bare paste; b keeps the noise. Recommended by the consultant, not owner-typed.
